string-array.name: mode_blurbs
string-array.item: ATSC 8-VSB, 6 MHz channel (the DVB-only settings are off)
ATSC 3.0 (NextGen TV), 6 MHz channel, ROUTE services
ISDB-T (Japan, Brazil and most of South America; 8 MHz channels in the Maldives), 6, 7 or 8 MHz channel, 13 segments
DVB-S, DVB-S2 and DVB-S2X satellite TV (L-band IF through an LNB)
DTMB / DTMB-A digital TV (China, Hong Kong, Cuba), 8 or 6 MHz channel
DVB-C cable TV (EN 300 429 / J.83 annex A and C): 16 to 256-QAM, symbol rate measured or set; needs a cable feed
Analogue TV: PAL, SECAM and NTSC with FM sound
MAC television (D2-MAC, D-MAC): the 1980s-90s European satellite TV, FM, about 27 MHz wide (20 Msps sees most of it)
DAB / DAB+ digital radio, Band III channels 5A to 13F
FM broadcast radio (87.5 - 108 MHz), stereo and RDS
DRM30 and DRM+ digital radio (shortwave, medium wave, VHF)
HD Radio (NRSC-5) digital sidebands of FM and AM stations (USA)
CDR (China Digital Radio) OFDM digital radio in the FM band
ADS-B / Mode S: aircraft on 1090 MHz
Mode S uplink: the 1030 MHz interrogations of radars and ACAS (Mode A/C, intermode, UF0 to UF24); needs 8 Msps
ACARS aircraft data link messages around 131 MHz
VDL Mode 2: the aircraft data link on 136.725 to 136.975 MHz, every channel at once
HFDL: the HF aircraft data link (ARINC 635), 3 to 22 MHz, every channel in the band at once
Airband AM voice, 118 to 137 MHz: several 25 and 8.33 kHz channels at once
VOR navigation beacons, 108 to 118 MHz: the radial, the identification and a position from two stations
ILS approach guidance: localizer 108.10 - 111.95 MHz, glide slope 329 - 335 MHz, marker beacons on 75 MHz

NDB (non-directional beacon) on long wave, 190-535 kHz: the Morse ident of an aeronautical beacon (a keyed 400 Hz or 1020 Hz tone, or a keyed carrier, about 7 WPM). Receive only. Not the HF beacon list

Drone Remote ID (ASTM F3411 / ASD-STAN EN 4709-002 Open Drone ID) on 2.4 GHz: Bluetooth LE advertising and Wi-Fi beacons at once; serial number or session ID, UA type, position, height, speed and track, operator position and ID, on a table and a map (receive only: Remote ID is a public broadcast meant for anyone to read; nothing is transmitted)
AIS ship transponders on 161.975 and 162.025 MHz

VDES (VHF Data Exchange System, ITU-R M.2092): ASM messages on 161.975 / 162.025 MHz decoded (GMSK 9.6 kbit/s, AIS framing, CRC checked); VDE-TER bursts on the 157.2 and 161.8 MHz channels detected with bandwidth, level and modulation class (frames not decoded)
NAVTEX navigational and weather warnings to ships, 518 kHz (SITOR-B)
DSC digital selective calling: distress alerts and calls, MF/HF and VHF channel 70
HF weather fax (radiofax): weather charts for ships on upper sideband
GNSS satellites (GPS, GLONASS, BeiDou, Galileo) around 1575 MHz, needs an active antenna
Inmarsat-C satellite messages (EGC safety and news broadcasts) near 1537.7 MHz
Inmarsat Aero satellite data link: P channels at 600 and 1200 bit/s near 1545 MHz, and 10500 bit/s near 1546 MHz
Meteor-M N2-3 / N2-4 weather pictures on 137.1 / 137.9 MHz (LRPT: OQPSK or QPSK, 72 or 80 ksym/s): the MSU-MR channels and a colour composite grow line by line during the pass, saved as PNG

GOES-16 / 18 / 19 HRIT on 1694.1 MHz (BPSK 927 ksym/s, Viterbi, Reed-Solomon, CCSDS packets, LRIT files): full disk and mesoscale images (Rice, plain or JPEG) grow as their lines arrive, EMWIN weather text and admin messages, saved to a folder. Needs a dish (about 1 m, or a grid) with an LNA at the feed

Elektro-L N3 / N4 / N5 L-band weather: HRIT and LRIT on 1691 MHz (BPSK, Viterbi, Reed-Solomon, CCSDS / xRIT, the same product path as GOES) and GGAK space-weather PCM/PM on 1693 MHz at 5 ksym/s. Pick the spacecraft and the link. Needs a dish with an LNA. Receive only

HRPT / AHRPT weather satellite pictures near 1.7 GHz: MetOp-B / MetOp-C AHRPT (QPSK 2.33 Msym/s, 1701.3 MHz) with the AVHRR channels growing line by line, FY-3 AHRPT (about 2.8 Msym/s, frames counted only) and the retired NOAA HRPT (BPSK, Manchester, 665.4 kbit/s). Needs a dish (about 1 m or more, tracking the satellite) with an LNA at the feed and a fast radio (4 Msps or more: HackRF, Airspy, SDRplay, Pluto; not an RTL-SDR)
Orbcomm subscriber downlinks, 137.2 - 137.8 MHz: 4800 bit/s SDPSK, two downlinks at once, satellites and their ephemeris

QO-100 (Es\'hail-2) geostationary amateur satellite, 10489.5 - 10500 MHz through a Ku LNB: beacon lock corrects the LNB\'s error and drift, narrowband SSB listening, wideband DATV hand-over to DVB-S/S2

FLARM: glider and light-aircraft collision-avoidance broadcasts on 868.2 and 868.4 MHz (Europe), received like the Open Glider Network does. Old-protocol positions are decoded (device ID, type, altitude, speed, track, climb) and shown in a table and on the live map with distance and bearing from your receiver; the newer protocol is only counted. Receive only; aircraft that set the no-track or stealth flag are only counted, never shown or saved

DJI drones on 2.4 and 5.8 GHz, receive only: wideband OFDM burst trains are classified by their shape (OcuSync-like, Lightbridge-like, unknown wideband OFDM) from the width, burst period, duty cycle and cyclic-prefix correlation, with a confidence and a clear note that this is a guess from the signal shape; DJI DroneID (the OcuSync 2 broadcast: Zadoff-Chu roots 600 and 147, turbo code, CRC-24) is decoded to the drone\'s serial number, position, home point and pilot position as sent in the clear. Needs 16 Msps or more (HackRF at 20 Msps; Pluto, bladeRF, USRP). The encrypted video link is never decoded

CubeSat telemetry from amateur satellites on 2 m / 70 cm (145.8 - 146 and 435 - 438 MHz): AX.25 at 1200 baud AFSK and 9600 baud G3RUH, GOMspace AX100 Mode 5 (ASM + Golay + Reed-Solomon) and Mode 6, CCSDS Reed-Solomon frames; callsigns, hex and ASCII dumps, satellite names from an editable table, KISS out to SatNOGS-style tools; the pass planner starts it with Doppler

Globalstar L-band downlink, 1610 - 1626.5 MHz: activity monitor only (receive only, the spread and encrypted content is not decoded): power, occupancy and Doppler of the 13 CDMA channels, an event log, and a pass overlay from the pass planner\'s TLEs
DMR two-slot digital voice and data, 12.5 kHz channel
NXDN digital two-way radio: NXDN48 (6.25 kHz) and NXDN96 (12.5 kHz), conventional and trunked
APCO Project 25 Phase 1 (TIA-102) digital two-way radio, C4FM, 12.5 kHz: conventional channels and trunked control channels
dPMR (ETSI TS 102 490) digital two-way radio, 6.25 kHz: PMR446 digital channels 1 to 16 (446.1 - 446.2 MHz) and the licensed bands
TETRA base stations (ETSI EN 300 392): network code, colour code, location area, carriers, neighbour cells, services and whether encryption is used (receive only, public broadcast, nothing decrypted)

TETRAPOL (not TETRA) base stations, GMSK 8 kbit/s on 10 / 12.5 kHz UHF channels (PAS 0001-2): D_SYSTEM_INFO gives country, system, cell, location area and scramble. Receive only, no voice, nothing decrypted
LTE cells around you: operator, band, EARFCN, PCI, eNB and sector, TAC, neighbours (receive only, public broadcast)

5G NR cells around you from their SS/PBCH blocks on the sync raster (GSCN) of n1, n3, n7, n8, n20, n28, n38, n40, n41, n77, n78: PCI, SSB index / beam, SS-RSRP / RSRQ / SINR, MIB (SFN, subcarrier spacing, k_SSB, CORESET#0, barred) (receive only, public broadcast)

LTE NB-IoT cells around you (180 kHz carriers, in-band, guard band or standalone) from their NPSS / NSSS, NPBCH (MIB-NB) and SIB1-NB: PCI, operating mode, antenna ports, SFN, operator (MCC / MNC), tracking area, cell identity, band, level; band scan over the 100 kHz raster. Receive only: the public broadcast only, nothing addressed to a device is decoded
Railway GSM base stations (GSM-R, 921 - 925 MHz): cell identity, location area, operator, channel lists (receive only, public broadcast)
LBJ (Chinese railway train proximity warning) on about 821.2375 MHz: FM voice channel with 1200 bit/s FSK data for train number, kilometre marker, locomotive ID, direction and speed (receive only)
POCSAG paging messages (512, 1200 and 2400 bd) on a 25 kHz channel
FLEX paging messages (1600, 3200 and 6400 bit/s) on a 25 kHz channel
Everyday 433.92, 868 and 915 MHz devices: weather stations, tyre pressure sensors, remotes, energy and water meters, Z-Wave (passive; S0 and S2 stay encrypted)

LoRaWAN monitor, EU868 (868.1 / 868.3 / 868.5 MHz) or US915, SF7 - SF12: message types, DevAddr and network, frame counters, MAC commands, join requests (only the clear headers; payloads stay encrypted)
Meshtastic LoRa mesh messages, positions and telemetry (868 and 915 MHz bands)
MeshCore LoRa mesh adverts and messages (868 and 915 MHz bands)
Bluetooth Low Energy advertising on channels 37, 38 and 39 (2402 / 2426 / 2480 MHz): device names, vendors, services, iBeacon and Eddystone, like a scanner app (receive only: never connects or pairs)

Zigbee and IEEE 802.15.4 on the 2.4 GHz channels 11 - 26 (O-QPSK, 2 Mchip/s, 250 kbit/s): networks (PAN ID, extended PAN ID, coordinator), devices with vendor from the address, MAC / NWK / APS headers, beacons and commands, a live frame log; channel scan. Receive only: encrypted payloads are not decrypted (the network key is not obtainable), only frames sent in the clear are shown. Needs a fast radio (4 Msps or more), not an RTL-SDR

Wi-Fi HaLow (802.11ah) networks in the sub-GHz bands, 863 - 868 MHz in Europe and 902 - 928 MHz in the US: S1G beacons at 1, 2 and 4 MHz channel widths give the SSID, BSSID, vendor, channel, bandwidth, MCS, level and the security type the network announces (information only). EU and US channel presets and a channel scan. Receive only: nothing is sent or joined and nothing is decrypted. A 1 or 2 MHz channel works from 2.4 Msps (an RTL-SDR), 4 MHz needs a radio with 4 Msps or more

Datawell Waverider wave-buoy telemetry on HF, 25.5 - 35.5 MHz (up to 45 MHz on request), heard as a USB signal. The 2FSK format of the DWR-MkIII, DWR-G and WR-SG buoys (81.92 bit/s) is decoded from Datawell\'s published reference manual: heave / north / west displacements, wave height and period, water temperature, GPS position and the 64 band directional spectrum, with the buoy\'s error-correcting code repairing bit errors. The 4FSK format of the DWR4 (163.84 bit/s) is not public: only the carrier, its tones and measurements of the bit stream are shown. Listed channel presets. Receive only

CODAR SeaSonde, WERA and similar coastal HF ocean radars: the FMCW sweeps in the 4.4 - 4.65, 5.25, 12 - 14, 24.45 - 24.65 and 41.5 - 42.5 MHz bands, found as moving lines in the spectrum: centre, sweep width, rate, direction, repetition and level, a table of the radars heard with first / last heard and SNR history, a chirp waterfall with the sweeps marked, the band and time each was heard (propagation, no position claimed), band presets and a scan over the radar bands. The Morse call sign some radars send is decoded from the keyed sweep width and always labelled unverified. Receive only: broadcast radar, nothing is decrypted

Multitone Electronics (UK) pagers, Mk IV to VII, in hospitals and industrial sites, 25 - 470 MHz, narrowband FM with FFSK: a detector, not a decoder, because the format is not public. Per transmission: the carrier, the FM deviation, the steady tones and spectral lines of the audio and, when the audio is two-level FSK, the measured baud rate, the bit stream in hex and how many 32-bit words pass the POCSAG BCH(31,21) check, with the POCSAG sync word flagged. Everything is labelled unverified; no message text is shown. Receive only: pager messages are private, nothing is decrypted or transmitted

NOAA Weather Radio (US and Canada) SAME / EAS alerts on the seven narrow-FM weather channels, 162.400 - 162.550 MHz: the 520.83 baud AFSK header sent three times is voted bit by bit and every field checked, then shown in plain English: originator, event (tornado warning, severe thunderstorm warning, required weekly test and the rest of the EAS table), the locations with the partial-county direction, valid for, issue time and sender call sign, how many of the three repeats agreed, the 1050 Hz attention tone, an alert history and a map of the states and provinces named (approximate). County names come only from a county table you load (none are built in). Receive only: the text of an alert is a public broadcast

ANT+ sensors on 2457 MHz (and other ANT networks on their own channel): heart rate straps and watches, bike speed, cadence and power sensors, footpods, environment sensors, as a watch or bike computer hears them: 1 Mbit/s GFSK frames with the device number, type and the data page, the heart rate with the beat count and R-R interval plotted over time, power, cadence, speed, temperature, manufacturer, serial and battery pages. Receive only: nothing is sent, paired or acknowledged, and only the open broadcasts are shown. Needs a radio that reaches 2.4 GHz at 4 Msps (HackRF, Pluto, LimeSDR, BladeRF, USRP).

DECT cordless phones and base stations on the ten carriers 1881.792 - 1897.344 MHz (Europe; 1.152 Mbit/s GFSK, 10 ms frames of 24 slots): every base station from the beacon it sends every frame, with its RFPI (the manufacturer code and system number inside it), level and the slots it uses, the system information tails and a burst log with base and handset bursts. Activity and signalling only: calls are encrypted and the voice is not decoded, nothing is transmitted. Needs a radio that reaches 1.9 GHz at 5 Msps or more (HackRF, Pluto, LimeSDR, BladeRF, USRP, SDRplay).

Plain LoRa between two radios (point to point, not LoRaWAN, not a mesh): every frame as bytes (hex and text) with SNR, level and carrier offset. You set the spreading factor (SF5 - SF12), bandwidth (125 / 250 / 500 kHz), coding rate and CRC (implicit header), header mode and sync word, or leave the spreading factor and bandwidth on Auto and every combination is searched. EU868, US915 and 433 MHz presets. Receive only: nothing is sent, decrypted or interpreted

Wi-Fi access points on 2.4 GHz channels 1 - 13 from their beacons (802.11b DSSS, 1 Mbit/s): SSID, BSSID and vendor, channel, security (open, WEP, WPA, WPA2, WPA3), rates, beacon interval and level, like a phone\'s Wi-Fi list (passive: beacons only, never joins or transmits)
Weather balloon radiosondes, 400 to 406 MHz (RS41, DFM, M10 and others)

Time and frequency stations: DCF77 (77.5 kHz), MSF and WWVB (60 kHz), JJY (40 / 60 kHz), WWV / WWVH (2.5 - 20 MHz): the time, date, summer time and leap second flags, the seconds tick, and how far the computer clock is off after the path delay

HF chirp sounders (ionosondes and oblique sounders, 0 - 30 MHz at 100 - 500 kHz/s): sweeps found by dechirping, their rate, period and start offset, an ionogram of group range against frequency, a timeline, PNG / CSV export; no decoder
Radio astronomy: the 21 cm hydrogen line (1420.4058 MHz) and the OH lines; long integration, on - off reference, baseline fit, radial velocity, drift-scan waterfall, CSV export; no decoder
FT8 weak-signal contacts in 15 s slots, 14.074 MHz
FT4 contest mode in 7.5 s slots, 14.080 MHz
WSPR propagation beacons in 2 minute slots, 14.0956 MHz
JT65 weak-signal contacts (65-FSK, Reed-Solomon, 60 s periods, sub-modes A, B, C), 14.076 MHz
JT9 weak-signal contacts (9-FSK, convolutional code, 60 s periods, 15 Hz wide), 14.078 MHz
Q65 (A to E, 15 s to 5 min periods) for EME, scatter and weak-signal work: Q-ary repeat-accumulate code, 65-FSK
FST4 and FST4W (15 s to 30 min periods, 4-GFSK, LDPC (240,101) / (240,74)) for LF, MF and HF weak-signal contacts and beacons
MSK144 meteor scatter (72 ms frames, 2000 baud, 15 s periods): decodes the short bursts of meteor trails
PSK31 / PSK63 keyboard chat (BPSK and QPSK): every signal in the 3 kHz passband at once, 14.070 MHz
JS8Call keyboard messaging (8-FSK, normal / fast / turbo slots): heartbeats, directed messages, relays, 14.078 MHz
RTTY teletype (45.45 bd, 170 Hz shift) on upper sideband, 1 to 30 MHz
CW (Morse) skimmer: every signal in a 14 kHz window, 5 to 50 WPM, on the HF CW segments
SSTV slow-scan TV pictures (Martin, Scottie, Robot, PD) on upper sideband
HamDRM / EasyPal digital SSTV: pictures as files over DRM-style OFDM in 2.3 or 2.5 kHz of upper sideband, 14.233 MHz
Olivia MFSK keyboard mode with Walsh-Hadamard coding, weak-signal text, 14.1065 MHz
Contestia (Olivia with 6-bit characters, upper case, faster), 14.1095 MHz
MFSK4 to MFSK64 keyboard modes (MFSK16 is the usual one) with forward error correction, 14.0785 MHz
THOR keyboard modes (4 to 100) with incremental frequency keying and FEC, 14.077 MHz
DominoEX keyboard modes (4 to 22) with incremental frequency keying, 14.0715 MHz
Hellschreiber (Feld Hell, Slow Hell, Hell 80, HellX5): text as a picture of dots, 14.063 MHz
FreeDV digital voice (700D, 700E, 1600) on upper sideband
M17 open digital voice and data (4FSK, 9 kHz), 2 m and 70 cm
D-STAR digital voice (GMSK 4800 bit/s, 6.25 kHz), 2 m and 70 cm
APRS and AX.25 packet radio (1200 bd AFSK), 144.800 MHz in Europe; LoRa APRS is its own entry
LoRa APRS on 70 cm, 433.775 MHz in Europe (SF12, 125 kHz)
MeshCom LoRa nodes on 70 cm, 433.175 MHz in Europe
HF ALE (2G, MIL-STD-188-141 / FED-STD-1045): 8-FSK link establishment calls, soundings, AMD messages and LQA on the HFN channels, 14.109 MHz

HF beacon propagation monitor: which NCDXF/IARU International Beacon Project beacons (18 beacons on 14.100, 18.110, 21.150, 24.930 and 28.200 MHz, 10 s slots), Australian Long Dashes and Russian single-letter beacons can be heard from here, by band, with SNR, distance and bearing, a great-circle map and 24 hour history; an editable beacon list; clicking a beacon tunes and listens

Open a recording (WAV, MP3 or other audio, or an IQ file: .cs8 .cu8 .cf32 .sigmf) and take the signal apart without a radio: waveform and spectrogram with cursors, peaks, bandwidth, SNR, symbol rate, bursts and a modulation guess, then demodulate a chosen band (AM, FM, SSB, CW, ASK, FSK, AFSK, PSK, MSK) and read the bits
Listen anywhere in the band: NFM, WFM (mono), AM, USB, LSB and CW, click the spectrum to tune, filter width, squelch, AGC, de-emphasis, S-meter and audio recording to WAV
Spectrum explorer: look around the band, measure carriers (bandwidth, power, SNR, symbol rate), sweep a range, LNB offsets, bookmarks; no decoder
Wide sweeping spectrum analyser (1 - 6000 MHz in about a second with a HackRF): live, peak-hold and averaged traces, waterfall, markers, band overlay, CSV export
